PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-05
49M, ambulatory follow-up encounter.

S:
Patient returns for a follow-up visit. He reports feeling generally well but describes several weeks of intermittent joint aches in the hands and wrists with morning stiffness and a sun-sensitive facial rash, prompting further workup today. He takes his blood pressure medication each morning and checks home readings twice a week. He works as a landscaper and spends much of the day outdoors. Appetite is good and sleep is adequate. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 184 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: mild redness over sun-exposed skin of the face.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: mild tenderness at the wrists and small joints of the hands, no effusion, full range of motion.
Skin: faint sunburn-like redness over the cheeks.
Labs (this week): basic metabolic panel normal, CBC within normal limits, ANA negative, urinalysis unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/78. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Rule out lupus; ANA negative. Facial redness fits sun exposure and the joint aches fit repetitive hand use; no further autoimmune testing or rheumatology referral needed. Advised strict sun protection and protective clothing at work.
3. Supportive care: discussed joint protection and over-the-counter measures for comfort.

Return in 3 months, sooner if the rash spreads or new joint swelling develops.
